name: Atolla jelly
fact: Some Atolla jellies produce a flashing display when disturbed. The display is thought to attract a larger predator that may attack the jelly's attacker: a burglar-alarm defense.
observe: Watch the bell contract and the trailing tentacles. The colored glow in this prototype is an artistic interpretation, not its everyday appearance.

name: Dumbo octopus
habitat: Deep ocean · often near the seafloor
fact: Dumbo octopuses are named for the ear-like fins on their mantle. They use those fins and their webbed arms to move through the water. Different species occupy different depths.
observe: Look for the paired fins and the web between the arms. Our simplified model exaggerates their silhouette; its glow is artistic.

name: Giant isopod
fact: Giant isopods are crustaceans related to the woodlice found on land. They scavenge food that reaches the seafloor. Species differ in size and geographic range.
observe: Observe the segmented body, antennae, and legs. Food can be scarce in the deep sea; a scavenger must take opportunities when they arrive.
